sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Warren, Ohio?
sections.html:
Warren is the seat of Trumbull County, on the Mahoning River about 14 miles northwest of Youngstown and 56 miles southeast of Cleveland. Selling here means working with a city whose rules for rentals, vacant houses and contractors are written into its Codified Ordinances.

The Census Bureau estimates 38,328 residents for July 1, 2025. That is below the 39,201 counted in 2020 and the 41,557 counted in 2010. Whether you hold an inherited house, a rental or a vacant property, the sections below cover the local and county steps that apply.

sections.h2: How did Warren's industrial past shape its housing?
sections.html:
The town was founded in 1798 on land bought from the Connecticut Land Company and became the Trumbull County seat in 1801. By 1888 four railroads served it. Packard Electric and Packard Motor Car were both founded in Warren in the 1890s, and steel became a major industry across the county through the 20th century. The Trumbull Steel mill, later part of Republic Steel, kept running under various owners until 2012.

Population followed the mills. Warren peaked at 63,494 in 1970 and has fallen in every census since, to 46,832 in 2000 and 39,201 in 2020. Many late 19th and early 20th century buildings still stand around Courthouse Square. The larger employers now include St. Joseph Warren Hospital, the Tribune Chronicle and Thomas Steel Strip, and Kimberly-Clark announced plans in 2024 for a new paper production facility in the city.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about owning in Warren?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 show a city where renters and low values define the market.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 56.1%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $86,400.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $967 with a mortgage and $409 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $766.
  • Households: 16,871, at 2.16 people per household.
  • Median household income: $37,887; persons in poverty: 31.9%.

With values in this range, the cost of repairs is a large share of the price, so buyers weigh condition closely and expect the seller to say what is wrong.

sections.h2: Does a Warren rental need a dwelling permit?
sections.html:
Yes. Under section 1367.10 of Warren's Codified Ordinances, no dwelling unit that lacks at least one owner living in it can be occupied without a residential non-owner occupied dwelling permit from the Health Officer's office. The permit is issued after a Building Inspector confirms compliance with the Housing, Building, Zoning and fire codes.

  • The annual fee for a single-unit dwelling is $120, and multi-unit buildings pay $100 per unit for two to fifty units, with lower per-unit rates above that.
  • A permit lasts one year and cannot be transferred to a new owner, so a buyer of a tenant-occupied house has to apply in their own name.
  • The Water Department will not open service for a non-owner-occupied unit without proof of the permit.
  • Occupying a unit without a permit carries a $1,000 fine, and each day counts as a separate violation.

If you are selling a rental, ask the Health Department whether the permit is current before listing, and tell the buyer the permit does not travel with the deed.

sections.h2: When does an empty Warren house count as vacant?
sections.html:
Chapter 1338 sets up a Vacant Property Registry. An owner has 30 days after a structure becomes vacant to register it with the Code Official. The annual fee is $200 for a residential structure, though it can be avoided if the property is secured, free of trash, mowed, and shows a visible address. Missing the filing deadline costs $50 per day up to $1,000.

One rule bears directly on a sale. A house listed with a real estate broker under a signed listing agreement is not treated as vacant for the first six months of that listing. An unoccupied house listed for sale by owner is treated as vacant from the start. If you plan to sell without a broker and have moved out, register or secure the property first.

sections.h2: Do you need a contractor to fix up a Warren house before selling?
sections.html:
Not always. Chapter 1305 requires contractors working on buildings in the city to register with a $25,000 surety bond, workers' compensation proof and liability insurance, but it does not apply to a homeowner doing work on a single-family dwelling they live in. That owner can file a waiver of liability with the Building Division, and permits under Chapter 1307 still apply.

Anyone hired to do the work has to hold a city registration first, and a contractor who starts without one pays double the registration fee. Ask any contractor for the city registration before work begins.

sections.h2: How does the Trumbull County Board of Revision work?
sections.html:
The Auditor, Treasurer and County Commissioners (or their representatives) sit as the Board of Revision. It hears value complaints, homestead and owner-occupancy disputes, and some penalty remission requests, and it does not touch the tax dollars on your bill. The burden of proof sits with the person who filed.

  • File with the Trumbull County Auditor, acting as secretary to the board, by email at BOR@co.trumbull.oh.us, by mail, in person or by fax. Forms filled out by hand need a notary; forms completed on a computer and emailed do not.
  • Useful evidence includes an independent appraisal, photos, repair estimates and, after a recent sale, the settlement statement and purchase agreement.
  • Hearings can be attended in person, by phone or by video, and notice comes at least ten days ahead.
  • A decision can be appealed to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days of the decision letter.

Under Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 the window closes March 31 of the year after the tax year. A third party may challenge a value upward only if an arm's length sale beat the listed value by ten percent and by the state threshold, which the county page puts at $567,000 for tax year 2025.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks stay with the owner in Trumbull County?
sections.html:
The county page describes a Homestead Exemption for owners 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or a surviving spouse who was at least 59 when the exemption holder died. The reduction is up to $29,000 of market value, and the income cap for applications covering 2026 taxes payable in 2027 is $41,000 of Ohio adjusted gross income. Veterans who are 100% permanently disabled from service may receive up to $58,000 with no income cap.

Owner Occupancy gives a reduction of about 2.5% to those who live in the home, on one acre and the house. Both benefits end when you sell, so a buyer starts without them.

sections.h2: What does Ohio require when you sell an inherited house?
sections.html:
Many Warren sales begin with an estate. Under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30, a seller who acquired the house by inheritance and has not lived in it within the past year does not have to deliver the state disclosure form. A fiduciary selling for an estate, a guardianship or a trust is exempt as well. Everyone else selling a one-to-four unit home must hand over the signed form.

Even when the form is not required, a buyer will ask about known defects. Answer in writing and keep a copy.

sections.h2: How do Warren's roads and winters affect showing a house?
sections.html: A freeway carrying Ohio 82 bypasses the city, and Ohio 5 leads southwest to the Ohio Turnpike. US 422 and Ohio 45 also run through Warren. NOAA normals reproduced for the city list 40.81 inches of precipitation and 27.9 inches of snow per year, with 21 snowy days and a January mean minimum of 16.8 degrees. Plan showings around plowed walks, working heat and visible roof and gutter condition, since buyers check these first in winter.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a rental house in Warren?
faqs.a: The seller needs no sale permit, but the rental dwelling permit under section 1367.10 does not transfer. The buyer applies for a new one, and the Water Department wants proof of it before opening service.

faqs.q: What if I move out and list the house myself?
faqs.a: An unoccupied house listed for sale by owner counts as vacant under Chapter 1338 and must be registered within 30 days. Under that chapter a broker-listed house is exempt for the first six months of the listing.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to dispute my property value in Trumbull County?
faqs.a: March 31 of the year after the tax year, or the first-half collection date if later. The tax year 2025 window closed March 31, 2026. Call the Auditor at 330-675-2420.

faqs.q: Does an inherited house need the Ohio disclosure form?
faqs.a: Usually no. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 excuses a seller who inherited the property and has not occupied it within a year, and it excuses fiduciaries acting for an estate.

faqs.q: Can I keep my homestead exemption after I sell?
faqs.a: No. The exemption attaches to the home you own and live in as of January 1, so it ends with the sale. A new home needs its own application with the county auditor.
